title: Bud's band grows to 18; first dance and Bud's big voice
summary: The band grew with new horn players, played country clubs and parties, got its first dance from Mrs. Poole, and Bud's huge singing voice carried over the river.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And from then, well, he had chased away from home for a while and came back and met lots of musicians, different places, and he looked over the billboard and we would get in. Next was a trombone and there's a trumpet player. And on and, you know, like that, till the band got to about 18 strong. And we never had been out no more than just serenading and playing for little country clubs and little dances like that. Mrs. Trevi Poole was a white lady of us dancing school. She gave us our first dance here in Natchez. I think at the Institute Hall. And we made a dollar man that night. And we thought that that was just lots of money. And from there we serenading, serenading around amongst every night then to be a bunch of white gentlemen and ladies would get us to go for little parties and things. And he was just a gifted singer. I imagine it just came to him just, he was, he could thunder. Absolutely. He could sing. He'd be on the bluff and people would be dancing over the river. By his, he could just, he could sing. He'd sing a few little, little old small megaphone, you know.

Yes, like that. He wasn't awful. It had to have been this. No telling you, you're going to hurt him in New Orleans. And so that's the way the band began to, then he began to play in Vidalia, to Ferdy, St.
Joe, Newton, and all around in a different place like that.
